correctness.rationale: For M>=3 over C, the three pairwise scalar products are a prime complete-intersection ideal (Casabella–Sammartano Theorems 1–2 give D_prime(3)=3, or Xie's strict M>2 theorem), hence dim=3M-3. A dependence of their Jacobian rows corresponds to nonzero hollow symmetric 3x3 Lambda with V Lambda=0. A nonzero hollow symmetric 3x3 has rank>=2, so rank(V)>=2 is smooth. If V=w(c1,c2,c3) has rank one, its dependency determinant is -2c1c2c3: singular precisely when some ci=0. Exactly one nonzero ci lies in one of three M-planes; two nonzero ci imply w is isotropic and give one of three irreducible rank-one Segre cones of dimension M. Their projective forms are P1 x Q^(M-2) under O(1,1); degree=2(M-1), giving reduced singular-locus degree 3+6(M-1)=6M-3. At generic linear-plane point solve two normal equations and retain a nondegenerate pairing on w-perp x w-perp; at generic isotropic cone solve two independent linear equations and retain nondegenerate pairing on w-perp x ker(ell). Formal Morse with parameters gives an ordinary quadratic hypersurface of 2M-2 variables times M smooth directions. I independently checked exact ranks 2 and 2M-2 at both representative component types for M=3,4,5. No conclusion about the scheme-theoretic Jacobian nilpotents or component intersections.
